title: Denmark Confronts a Stark Choice: Guns · 12 Oct
keywords: Denmark, defence spending, NATO, welfare state, vocational education, skills shortage, GDP, inflation, green transition, Nordic model, European security, hybrid threats, public spending, labour market, apprenticeships
notes: Denmark is preparing to raise defence spending to 3.5 percent of GDP by 2030, a commitment that will reshape national priorities and force difficult questions about the future of the welfare state. At the same time, a cross-party deal to invest nearly one billion Danish kroner annually in vocational training is testing whether the country can build the skilled workforce its ambitions require. Together, the two debates expose a fundamental tension at the heart of the Nordic model: how much security and economic transformation can a society purchase before the bill arrives at the welfare office.
